answer: At dawn on a named knoll, a newcomer weighs the dew on one mirror plate before two witnesses, and the yield must match its two neighbouring knolls within a gram. A plate weighed late, or dew poured in from a bottle, voids the claim and burns a 450 POA bond, barring re-entry six epochs. Each plate costs $110 plus a $40 weighing fee, so 100 fakes need 100 plates at $15,000 and 45,000 POA in bonds, while honest collectors weigh real mornings.
